headline: Across media, gaming, publishing and education firms are balancing cost cuts with selective tech investments amid mixed performance.
summary: Media giants posted revenue growth but are tightening IT spend and pursuing AI pilots. Gaming operators show strong top‑line gains for some players while tightening budgets overall. Publishers are expanding digital and AI capabilities despite mixed earnings. Education providers are split between growth at Pearson and cost reductions at SLU.

industries.summary: Disney posted 8% revenue growth and a 43% jump in operating income but is targeting $3 bn cost savings. WBD/Skydance saw modest revenue growth and cost‑cutting measures. Versant is expanding digital platforms while maintaining positive sentiment.

leaders.why: Highest quarterly revenue (25,947 m) and strong operating margin (19.2%).

laggards.why: Low operating margin (5.2%) and revenue decline YoY (-2.3%).

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: Multiple firms announced large‑scale savings programs and staff buyouts.

themes.title: AI & tech pilots
themes.detail: Executives highlighted AI use in parks and future technology initiatives.

industries.it_note: IT budgets are being constrained as companies prioritize cost reductions, though selective AI projects receive funding.

industries.summary: Caesars posted record revenue but widened its net loss, while Bally's delivered 22.8% revenue growth and is expanding its digital platform. Light & Wonder and Brightstar maintain stable margins but are tightening spend.

leaders.why: Revenue up 21.7% YoY to 807.6 m and positive sentiment.

laggards.why: Widened net loss of $123 m despite revenue growth.

themes.title: Digital rebuild
themes.detail: Bally's integrates Intralot systems; Brightstar launches next‑gen lottery solutions.

themes.title: Cost control
themes.detail: Light & Wonder focuses on debt reduction; Caesars emphasizes AI will not replace face‑to‑face meetings.

industries.it_note: IT spending is being trimmed across operators, with digital upgrades funded selectively.

industries.summary: Pearson shows accelerated revenue growth and an expanding IT outlook. Scholastic missed revenue targets and posted a large operating loss. Wolters Kluwer is investing in AI partnerships and acquisitions.

leaders.why: Revenue of 1,779 m and improving operating margin (14.2%).

laggards.why: Revenue miss of 216.8 m and deep operating loss (-42.5%).

themes.title: M&A & AI
themes.detail: Wolters Kluwer acquires AgileMD and partners with Viz.ai; Pearson expands AI credentialing.

themes.title: Cost restructuring
themes.detail: Pearson announced a major business restructure to improve margins.

industries.it_note: Publishers are increasing IT spend to support AI integration and digital acquisitions.

industries.summary: Pearson continues to grow revenue and expand IT, while SLU cuts costs through staff layoffs and outsourcing. NYU pilots a shuttle‑bus service with no clear IT direction.

leaders.why: Strong revenue (1,779 m) and expanding IT outlook.

laggards.why: Entire custodial staff laid off and services outsourced, indicating tightening spend.

themes.title: Cost‑cutting
themes.detail: SLU outsources custodial services; Pearson restructures business units.

themes.title: AI adoption
themes.detail: Pearson’s Credly platform sees rapid AI credential growth.

industries.it_note: IT investment is expanding at Pearson but tightening at SLU; overall outlook remains uncertain.
